correctness.rationale: Every \(n\)-symbol word has one exact affine periodic response, with denominator \(1-(-b)^{n/\gcd(n,2)}\), so the finite symbolic branch inequalities are necessary and sufficient. The 358-word exhaustive exact-rational certificate for \(n\le5\) at \(b=1/4\) yields four five-word classes, two admissible in \(0<d/h<1\) above \(205/252\), and no nontrivial shorter cycles. The explicit parametric expressions satisfy the recurrence and have strict branch margins throughout the stated open family. \(J^2=-bI\) proves attracting return multipliers of modulus \(b^{5/2}\); the origin also attracts locally. The actual standalone checker was executed and its precise scope is recorded; no long-period absence follows.

The 2024/2025 related paper uses the same piecewise-affine architecture after parameter scaling, and reports five-cycles numerically but its cycle analysis and stability propositions do not establish the exact \(d/h=205/252\) weak-forcing threshold or exhaustive shortest-period census. Direct claim-level comparison against the available indexed results and accessible prior mathematical claims found no covering equivalence. value.rationale: The source specifically leaves weak forcing \(d<h\) open; the result gives an exact natural border-collision onset, a certified complete primitive-period \(\le5\) census and simultaneous coexistence of two distinct attracting five-cycles with the stable fundamental equilibrium. The neutral branch is visited twice per cycle, unlike the source families. These sharp parameters and period multiplicities supply usable analytical benchmarks for detecting multistability in a discontinuous market dynamics model; the result does not rest on an arbitrary unmotivated sample or on a tiny numerical improvement.
